item.title: #3586696: Add the load_ai_context_items function call and deprecate load_ai_context_item_by_id
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 16 files, +886/−268 · php +779/−249 · md +107/−19
  • Diff: 65f20b7
  • Discussion: #3586696 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

The AI Context load tool has a new ID, ai_context:load_ai_context_items, because the old name load_ai_context_item_by_id did not match what the tool does (it loads one or more items) or the other two tool IDs. The new tool has the same inputs, access checks and output as before. The old ID stays as a deprecated alias until 2.0.0, so existing agents keep working. The agent tool list shows it as "Load AI Context Item By ID (deprecated)". New agents should use the new tool. Existing agent configuration is not migrated automatically. Agent prompts that name the old tool must be edited by hand.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: Agent configuration that names the old plugin ID (tools, default information tools, overrides) keeps working but should be changed by hand to the new ID. No update hook migrates it.
  • Deprecation: Function call plugin ID ai_context:load_ai_context_item_by_id is deprecated in 1.0.0 and removed in 2.0.0. Each call triggers E_USER_DEPRECATED.
  • New API: New function call plugin ID ai_context:load_ai_context_items (function name ai_context_load_ai_context_items, tool name "Load AI Context Items").

Technical details

The load logic moved out of LoadAiContextItemById into a new @internal abstract base class, AiContextLoadItemsFunctionCallBase. The new LoadAiContextItems plugin extends it with no overrides. LoadAiContextItemById also extends it, keeps its old id and function_name, and changes its name and description to say it is deprecated and name the new ID. Its execute() calls @trigger_error(..., E_USER_DEPRECATED) and then parent::execute(). The notice fires only when the tool runs. Listing the tools, building the agent form or creating the plugin does not trigger it. Both #[FunctionCall] attributes carry the same context_definitions, and the class docblock says to keep them in sync.

The docs (docs/developers/api-stability.md, function_calls.md, index.md, services.md) now use the new ID. api-stability.md lists the alias under "Deprecated APIs" and has an "Upgrade from 1.0.0-rc1: Load tool plugin ID" section. That section says to change default_information_tools entries and agent overrides to the new ID. It also says usage records still show the old ID for agents that have not been moved. A new kernel test, AiContextLoadFunctionCallAliasTest, checks that the definitions match, the output is identical for both IDs including the permission denial, and the deprecation fires only on execute. AiContextEchoAiSystemPromptTest gains a case that runs the old ID as a default information tool.

Upgrade

Replace the old plugin ID in agent config, using the same parameters:

tool: ai_context:load_ai_context_item_by_id

becomes

tool: ai_context:load_ai_context_items

This applies to the agent's tool selection and tool settings, its Default information tools, and any AI Agents agent overrides. Agent prompts that mention ai_context:load_ai_context_item_by_id or ai_context_load_ai_context_item_by_id must be edited by hand to use ai_context:load_ai_context_items or ai_context_load_ai_context_items. To find agents that still use the old ID, check the Tools used list on usage records.

item.title: #3586605: Correct the Language scope fail-open text and the conditional parent cap label
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 16 files, +171/−26 · php +151/−12 · md +20/−14
  • Diff: 45c39ec
  • Discussion: #3586605 · 1 contributor · 21 comments

Summary

Several help texts in AI Context described behavior the code does not have, and this fixes them. The Language scope text said an item is kept when the current language cannot be determined. That never happens, because a language is always detected. With no language prefix in the path, as in Drush, cron or queue calls, Drupal's negotiated content language is used, usually the site default. An item set only to other languages is therefore left out of those calls. The cap field "Max conditional parent decisions per request" is now labelled "per context resolution call", because one page request or agent run can make several resolution calls. Consumer form help now also names the Roles filter as a way items are left out. Behavior does not change, but the edited strings are translatable, so existing translations of them will need updating.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

This is a text and docs change only. AiContextLanguageService::detect() always returns a code, so AiContextScopeLanguage never produces a neutral (NULL) result for an item that has Language values. The corrected strings are in the AiContextScopeLanguage plugin description and getItemFormDescription(), in the Default row and Scope Subscriptions help in AiContextConsumerForm, and in the conditional_max_parents title and description in AiContextItemSettingsForm. The setting key, schema and AiContextSubcontextResolver limit logic are untouched.

Docs updated: docs/features/scopes.md (the Language example now says S also passes on a Spanish request, and explains the fallback), docs/features/subcontext.md, docs/developers/configuration.md, docs/developers/debugging.md (decision_cap_exhausted), plus multilingual.md and context_selection.md. These drop the claims that "detection happens once per request" and that Language "changes how it scores". The commit adds a kernel test, testRequestWithoutPrefixUsesNegotiatedLanguage(), and a second one for a non-default negotiated language. Functional tests are updated to assert the new strings.

item.title: #3586677: Getting a "AiContextSelector: Items cut off due to token limit: 4" warning and I don't understand why...
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 28 files, +1103/−100 · php +1023/−92 · md +79/−8 · yml +1
  • Diff: 8ccb883
  • Discussion: #3586677 · 1 contributor · 34 comments

Summary

The token figures shown for AI Context items now match what each item costs when injected. Before, the Tokens badge, its tooltip and the consumer budget summary counted only an item's guidance text. Items are actually injected as a block with an ID, label and purpose header and indented guidance. Items that looked like they fit within Max tokens for injection could still be cut off at render time. The "Items cut off due to token limit: 4" warning also now says what the number means: how many of the selected items did not fit, which token budget, which consumer, and the item IDs. After updating, run drush updatedb and drush cr. Expect higher badges, percentages and budget totals. Sites near their budget may now see Context budget exceeded. Selection and rendering behave as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: Update 10032 recounts the stored token_count of every ai_context_item revision and translation so it covers the rendered block.
  • Config change: No config schema change; the consumer budget summary note and the cut-off warning text are reworded.
  • New API: AiContextRendererInterface gains estimateItemTokens() and estimateBlockTokens(); AiContextTokenCountBackfillScheduler gains writeTokenCounts().

Technical details

AiContextItem::preSave() now stores AiContextRendererInterface::estimateItemTokens() in token_count instead of estimating the guidance text alone. That method calls the new estimateBlockTokens($id, $label, $purpose, $content), which builds the block with the same buildBlockPrefix() and buildBlock() helpers the renderer uses, so the stored figure and render() stay in step. The per-item figure excludes the blank separator between blocks. The context prefix and delimiters are added after the budget is enforced.

A new item has no ID in preSave(), so postSave() recounts it and writes the result through the new AiContextTokenCountBackfillScheduler::writeTokenCounts(). That writes straight to the column and avoids a second entity save. The recount check in the entity now also fires when the label or purpose changes. It also fires when a draft is published or an older revision is reverted to, because those carry whatever count they were saved with.

Update 10032 recounts through AiContextTokenCountBackfillScheduler::backfillChunk(), which now reads every revision and translation (from the revision data table when available) rather than only the current revision. It passes id, label, purpose and content to estimateBlockTokens(). If AiContextTokenizerUnavailableException is thrown, it calls deferRecount() so cron recounts later, as update 10023 does. The scheduler now takes @ai_context.renderer as a constructor argument.

The selector warning in AiContextSelector now uses @count, @selected and @max, plus @consumer when getConsumerId() is set. AiContextTokenEstimator::formatListingTooltip() gained a $children argument so a parent row says its figure already covers its subcontext items, which are listed separately. The budget summary note text in AiContextConsumerBudgetSummaryLazyBuilder was reworded.

Upgrade

Run the database update, then clear caches:

drush updatedb -y
drush cr

Update 10032 recounts every revision and translation in chunks. Code that decorates ai_context.renderer must implement the two new methods on AiContextRendererInterface (an @internal interface):

public function estimateItemTokens(AiContextItem $item): int;
public function estimateBlockTokens(string $id, string $label, string $purpose, string $content): int;

item.title: #3586645: Usage records and the invocation result count items that the token budget left out
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +655/−45 · php +604/−34 · md +51/−11
  • Diff: 4b0d01f
  • Discussion: #3586645 · 1 contributor · 25 comments

Summary

When a consumer's token budget is too small, the renderer shortens some context items and leaves others out. Before this fix, usage records and the generic-path invocation result still counted every selected item as delivered. The usage pages could then show an item as used by a consumer whose prompt never contained it. Now only items that reached the prompt are recorded and reported. A shortened item still counts as delivered, because part of it reached the model. An item the budget left out does not count.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Generic-path invocation result item_ids and item_count now contain only delivered items, so they can be smaller than the selection on sites with a tight token budget.
  • New API: AiContextSelectionResult::getOmittedItemIds() and getDeliveredItemIds(), plus AiContextSelectionTextRenderedEvent::getOmittedItemIds(), and an omitted_item_ids key in the renderer result.

Technical details

AiContextRenderer::render() now returns an omitted_item_ids list next to truncated_item_ids. It holds the IDs that produced no block at all: the budget had no room, or the entity could not be loaded or was unpublished. getTruncatedItemIds() is unchanged and still covers both shortened and dropped items, so an ID can appear in both lists. AiContextSelector passes the list into AiContextSelectionTextRenderedEvent (read-only, new trailing constructor argument omittedItemIds) and into AiContextSelectionResult.

AiContextSelectionResult::getDeliveredItemIds() returns getSelectedItemIds() minus the omitted IDs. AiContextBuildSystemPromptSubscriber (agent path) and AiContextPreGenerateResponseSubscriber (generic path) use it for recordUsage(). The generic path also uses it for the invocation result. getSelectedItemIds() is unchanged. The renderer decides what counts as delivered, so a TEXT_RENDERED subscriber that edits item text does not change the records.

The generic path still decides whether to push based on the selection, not on delivered items. If the budget leaves out every selected item but a TEXT_RENDERED subscriber added text, that text is pushed with status pushed, empty item_ids and item_count 0. In that case no usage is recorded. The docs (api-stability.md, consumer_api.md, usage_tracking.md) are updated, with a new "Beta upgrade: usage and item_ids count delivered items" section. A new kernel test covers both push paths, using a length-based test tokenizer so budgets can actually be exceeded.

Upgrade

Code that compared item_count or item_ids in the invocation result against its own selection count may now see fewer items. Use getSelectedItemIds() for what selection chose and getDeliveredItemIds() for what reached the prompt:

$result->getSelectedItemIds();   // unchanged
$result->getOmittedItemIds();    // left out completely
$result->getDeliveredItemIds();  // selected minus omitted

item.title: #3586648: Raise the default token budget for new sites to 20,000
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +33/−4 · php +22/−1 · md +10/−2 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: 7313146
  • Discussion: #3586648 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

New sites that install AI Context now get a default "Max tokens for injection" of 20,000, up from 1,200. The old value fit only one or two typical context items, so most sites had to raise it before the module was useful. Existing sites are not changed, because there is no update hook. Check the value at /admin/config/ai/context/settings/general. The budget applies to every pushed AI call, including each turn of an agent loop, so a higher value can raise input costs. Each consumer can override the budget under its own Advanced settings, either lower to limit cost or higher for more context.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: max_tokens in config/install/ai_context.settings.yml default raised from 1200 to 20000 for new installs; no update hook, existing sites keep their saved value.

Technical details

The default lives in two places that are set independently: config/install/ai_context.settings.yml (read on fresh install) and the AiContextSelection::DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS constant (the code fallback). Both are now 20000. A new unit test, testShippedMaxTokensMatchesTheConstant() in AiContextSelectionTest, decodes the install YAML and asserts it equals the constant, so the two cannot drift apart.

The docs were updated: the "default: 1200" text in docs/developers/configuration.md, the maxTokens example in docs/developers/services.md, and the consumer docs, which now explain the per-consumer override. The issue notes that the token budget ceiling in #3586636 defaults to 32,000, so it stays above the new default.

Upgrade

Existing sites keep their saved max_tokens. No update hook runs. To adopt the new default, raise Max tokens for injection at /admin/config/ai/context/settings/general. Code that relied on the AiContextSelection::DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS fallback of 1200 now gets 20000.

item.title: #3586687: Site Sections hard-filters on the supplied request path, but the selection's cache contexts carry only url.path and route
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +451/−5 · php +409/−3 · md +35/−2 · yml +7
  • Diff: 94fbdb7
  • Discussion: #3586687 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

AI Context selection results now vary by a new ai_context.request_path cache context. Site Sections filters on a path that can be supplied in a request attribute, a posted path parameter, a JSON body or a same-site Referer, not only the URL. Before this fix, two requests to one endpoint with different supplied paths could select different items but carry identical cache contexts. Custom code that cached a selection, or a render array built from one, could then serve items from the wrong site section. The module itself doesn't store selection results by cacheability, so the gap only affects custom consumers that cache them.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New ai_context.request_path cache context (cache_context.ai_context.request_path) holding the path that Site Sections filters on, now declared by the selector, the budget calculator and the detected language context.

Technical details

New AiContextRequestPathCacheContext (marked @internal), registered as cache_context.ai_context.request_path in ai_context.services.yml. Its getContext() returns AiContextRequestInfoResolver::getPath() or none, and its own cacheable metadata is empty.

The context is added to the contexts declared by AiContextSelector, to AiContextSubscriptionBudgetCalculator (its totals fingerprint reads the resolver's path), and to AiContextDetectedLanguageCacheContext::getCacheableMetadata() (language detection reads the same path for a language prefix). url.path and route are kept, because the resolver falls back to the URL and dropping url.path would change existing cache keys.

Docs: api-stability.md gets a "Caching a selection result" section. It says to compute cache keys in the same AI call, before AiContextRequestInfoResolver::resetRequestInfo() clears the supplied path or entity. It also warns that the supplied path is normalized but not validated against routes, so its cardinality is unbounded. Kernel tests cover the context's values (URI fallback, posted path, JSON path, same-site and cross-site Referer) and show that two body paths give different selections and different resolved cache keys.

Upgrade

Run drush cr so Drupal registers the new cache context. If custom code caches a selection result or a render array built from one, key it on all of the result's cache metadata (AiContextSelectionResult::getCacheableMetadata()), and don't drop url.path or route.

item.title: #3586661: Saving or rendering context items fails when the tiktoken vocab cannot be loaded
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 20 files, +2210/−63 · php +1953/−59 · md +237/−4 · json +15 · yml +5
  • Diff: f05a82c
  • Discussion: #3586661 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

AI Context no longer breaks when the tokenizer cannot load its vocabulary file. That file is downloaded on first use from openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net and cached in the Drupal temp directory. Before this fix, a blocked download, a non-writable temp directory or a corrupt cache file made item saves fail with "The changes could not be saved." It also stopped agent tools that load context. Now AI Context uses an approximate token count (bytes divided by 4), logs one warning, and keeps saving items, rendering context and answering agent requests. Stored counts are recalculated by cron once the vocabulary loads. Sites without outbound access can allow the host or copy the vocab file into the temp directory. The new docs describe both options.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: AiContextTokenEstimator::isTokenizerAvailable(), markTokenizerUnavailable() and reportEncodingFailure(), and AiContextTokenCountBackfillScheduler::queueDeferredRecount() and deferRecount().

Technical details

AiContextTokenEstimator::estimate() now catches \Throwable from setModel() and countTokens(). On failure it returns (int) ceil(strlen($text) / 4). The failure is remembered per model for UNAVAILABLE_CACHE_TTL (600 seconds), both in the service and in cache.default under ai_context:tokenizer_unavailable:{model}. Requests therefore do not retry the download, and drush cr clears the memo. One warning is logged per request to the ai_context channel. A text that fails to encode while the vocab is loaded gets an approximate count for that text only, and the tokenizer is not marked unavailable. The AI module's own cl100k_base fallback in Tokenizer::setModel() is uncaught, so the catch has to live in AI Context.

AiContextRenderer skips configureTextChunkerModel() when the tokenizer is unavailable and trims content with mb_strcut($content, 0, $max_tokens * 4) instead of TextChunker::chunkText(). It uses the same fallback if the chunker throws mid-render. While approximate counts are in use, the render result gets a max-age of 600 seconds, so cached output does not keep the byte-trimmed text after the vocab loads.

Fallback counts must not stay in storage permanently. AiContextItem::preSave() stores the approximate count and calls queueDeferredRecount(), which queues one full recount on ai_context_token_count_backfill. A state flag, ai_context.token_count_deferred_recount, limits this to one waiting recount. backfillChunk() checks isTokenizerAvailable() before counting and again before writing. When the tokenizer is unavailable it throws the @internal AiContextTokenizerUnavailableException and writes nothing. The queue worker turns that into SuspendQueueException. processQueuedChunk() releases the item and returns deferred: TRUE, and the settings-form batch shows a warning. backfillAll() and update 10023 call deferRecount() and finish instead of failing. Docs (services.md, configuration.md, debugging.md) were extended, and the kernel test base gained stubFailingTokenizerServices() with AiContextFailingTestTokenizer.

Upgrade

Sites that cannot reach the vocab host have two options. Allow outbound HTTPS to openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net, or copy the vocab file unchanged into the Drupal temp directory under the SHA-1 of its URL. The file for cl100k_base, which gpt-4 and unknown models use, is 9b5ad71b2ce5302211f9c61530b329a4922fc6a4. The file for o200k_base, used by gpt-4o models, is fb374d419588a4632f3f557e76b4b70aebbca790. Sites whose temp directory is emptied on each deploy can set $settings['file_temp_path'] to a persistent directory. After fixing the cause, run drush cr and then cron, so the approximate counts are recalculated.

  • Opened: October 24, 2026

item.title: #3586678: "Last used" value of "Context usage" table acts more like "first used" when used on new content entities
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +362/−5 · php +350/−1 · md +11/−4 · yml +1
  • Diff: a4d6b6a
  • Discussion: #3586678 · 1 contributor · 31 comments

Summary

The "Last Used" column on the Context usage page (/admin/config/ai/context/usage) now moves every time a context item is used. Before, a repeat use through the same consumer and route, such as CKEditor on a new node, stopped updating it after the second use, so it behaved like "first used". Usage cleanup on cron reads this value, so records still in use are no longer treated as old.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

"Last used" is the usage record's changed time. Core's ChangedItem only advances it when another field value differs, and a repeat use writes identical values. AiContextUsageTracker now takes datetime.time as a third constructor argument (wired in ai_context.services.yml). It calls setChangedTime($this->time->getRequestTime()) before every save() in recordUsage() (both the existing-record and new-record paths) and in attachEntity() (the paths that update the runner's record, update an existing entity record, and create a new record). The stamp is the request start time, so a long-running job records when it started.

The usage docs now say that Last Used is written on every use and that both cron cleanup rules (maximum age, then maximum record count) read Last Used rather than Created. Tests add a hand-moved clock, AiContextTestClock, swapped into the container's datetime.time. The kernel tests fail at the third use without the fix.

item.title: #3586620: Context items listing replaces its cache metadata instead of merging it
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +107/−7 · php +107/−7
  • Diff: 6d8826d
  • Discussion: #3586620 · 1 contributor · 28 comments

Summary

The AI Context items listing page now keeps all of its cache metadata. Before, parts of it were overwritten, so the list cache tag and the per-user cache contexts were dropped. On a default site this changes nothing, because admin routes are not stored in Dynamic Page Cache. It matters only if a site or later change makes this page cacheable. In that case, a new item might not show until caches were cleared, and on older Drupal core versions another user could be served the owner's Draft rows.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

AiContextItemListBuilder used CacheableMetadata::applyTo(), which assigns #cache instead of merging it. In render(), the settings config metadata overwrote the ai_context_item_list tag that core's EntityListBuilder::render() puts on $build['table']. The view-access metadata (listAccessCacheability) was then overwritten by scopeLabelCacheability, so the user context and the tags of hidden items were lost. The same pattern was in the settings-access code and in the tooltip helper that writes #cache on the child label cell.

Each call site now starts from CacheableMetadata::createFromRenderArray($build) (or $build['table']), adds the extra metadata with addCacheableDependency(), and applies the result once. Two kernel tests were added: testTableKeepsTheCoreListCacheTag and testViewAccessAndScopeLabelMetadataBothSurvive. The second checks that the user context, the hidden Draft's tag and the table tags are all present, and that another user's Draft is not in the rows. The issue notes that $build['#empty'] never renders; that was split out to #3586692 and is not part of this change.

item.title: #3586586: Update context items listing status filter to published and consumers listing push filter to on and add reset buttons
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +700/−144 · php +493/−106 · js +162/−29 · md +30/−9 · css +15
  • Diff: 072fbb4
  • Discussion: #3586586 · 1 contributor · 30 comments

Summary

The AI Context admin listings now open with useful defaults. The context items listing (/admin/config/ai/context/items) shows only Published items, and the consumers listing (/admin/config/ai/context/settings/consumers) shows only consumers with Automatic push On. Each listing has a Reset button that appears once a filter differs from its default. It restores the defaults and clears the search. If the default view is empty, the table says so and tells you to switch the filter to All. Without JavaScript the filter toolbar is hidden and every row stays visible.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Filtering stays client-side. The toolbars render with hidden, and the JS unhides them once it has applied the defaults. This is why a no-JS page shows every row.

Items listing: AiContextItemListBuilder now always renders the Status select with published preselected, even if no listed row is published. Published is matched through a new data-context-published row attribute (1 or 0), not the workflow state name, so custom workflow states that publish an item are covered. The remaining Status options are only the unpublished states seen on rendered rows. As a result, Published can still show unpublished relatives, such as a draft child of a published parent, because of the hierarchy-aware parent/child visibility.

Code that type-hints, implements or checks instanceof against any removed interface must switch to the concrete class. Tool result getters now return the concrete result classes. The interfaces were removed outright, without a deprecation period. The deprecated ExecutableResultInterface shell is also gone, so tools no longer pass instanceof ExecutableResultInterface checks.

The methods that used to come from ToolResultInterface and FormattedToolResultInterface keep their docblocks on the classes. ToolDefinition no longer implements TypedInputsDefinitionInterface or TypedOutputsDefinitionInterface, and its methods carry their own docs. The assert() calls in TypedInputsTrait and TypedOutputsTrait now check ToolDefinition. TextData no longer implements the empty TextInterface marker.

ToolInterface::getResult() and ToolInvocation::getResult() return ExecutableResult. ToolInterface::getFormattedResult() and ToolInvocation::getFormattedResult() return FormattedExecutableResult. item.title: #3586677: HostnameFilter handling of HTML in JSON
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +897/−56 · php +805/−56 · yml +78 · md +14
  • Diff: 619213b
  • Discussion: #3586677 · 1 contributor · 39 comments

Summary

The AI module's hostname filter treated JSON responses as HTML, so the result often no longer decoded. This hit structured output and any JSON built from HTML-containing strings, and some sites turned on full trust mode to get around it. Now JSON objects or arrays are detected and filtered one string at a time, so they stay valid JSON. A clean payload comes back unchanged, and only the strings that had a disallowed URL or unsafe markup are rewritten. Chat requests that set a structured output schema, streamed ones included, are filtered this way automatically. Callers can opt out with jsonMode: FALSE.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: No stored configuration changed. jsonMode is a per-request option on HostnameFilterDto.
  • New API: New jsonMode option on HostnameFilterDto, and HostnameFilter::setJsonMode(); structured output responses enable it automatically.

Technical details

HostnameFilter::filterText() now calls filterJsonText() before the Markdown and HTML5 round trip. It recognises text that is wholly a JSON object or array, or a single fenced block (``` or ~~~, json* tag, closing fence optional). Every string, keys included, is filtered through the new filterScalarString() and rewritten only if it changed. Numbers and whitespace stay as they were. Strings that are themselves JSON documents are handled recursively, up to depth 8. If the filtered raw text still reads as unsafe, for example when an escape such as \u0027 hides an attribute, the payload is re-encoded with <, >, & and quotes as \u escapes. If that still fails, the regular pipeline takes over.

filterHtmlLinks() now returns a bool saying whether it modified the tree. The HTML5 serializer output is used only when it did, so strings with a stray < or & are not entity-encoded. The unused processElements() helper was removed.

The new HostnameFilter::setJsonMode(), HostnameFilterDto::$jsonMode and the jsonMode key in snapshotSettings() and restoreSettings() cover text that does not decode, such as malformed or truncated JSON or a partial stream chunk. With jsonMode on, that text gets plain-text URL removal plus the DOM walk, and is rewritten only when something unsafe is found. ProviderProxy and StreamedChatMessageIterator turn it on for the duration of a call when ChatInput::getChatStructuredJsonSchema() is non-empty and the caller's DTO leaves jsonMode as NULL. They restore the singleton filter's settings afterwards. A streamed chunk is not decodable on its own, so a chunk that loses unsafe markup may no longer be valid JSON.

Related change: when a disallowed URL is removed in plain text, a trailing backslash is kept. That keeps the closing \" of a JSON string intact.

Upgrade

To opt out of the automatic JSON mode for a structured output request:

$input->setHostnameFilter(new HostnameFilterDto(jsonMode: FALSE));

Sites that enabled full trust mode only to keep JSON decodable can try removing it.

item.title: #3594881: Ask follow-up questions in one AI Answers conversation
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 22 files, +1073/−45 · php +959/−34 · md +89/−11 · yml +20 · json +5
  • Diff: f84130e
  • Discussion: #3594881 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

An AI Answers test can now ask a real follow-up question. Before, every question started a new AI Answers conversation, so a follow-up such as "Which courses does it include?" reached AI Answers without the earlier answer to refer to. A question can now set metadata.follow_up_of to the id of an earlier question. It is asked as the next turn of that question's conversation and graded as its own result. The result records follow_up_of and the turn number, and judges see the earlier questions and answers. A follow-up is skipped, with the reason on its result, when the question it follows is not in the run (for example with --question or --split), comes later in the dataset, failed, was skipped, or ran as another user. It is also skipped on engines that cannot continue a conversation, and on chat and agent targets. If you split a dataset with a hash rule, give every question in a chain the same split label, or the follow-up may be skipped.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: Datasets accept a new optional metadata.follow_up_of string, added to schema/dataset.schema.json.
  • New API: New WorkflowFollowUpInterface::releaseRun() for workflow runners that can continue a conversation, plus continueRunId and keepOpen on WorkflowRunOptions.

Technical details

AnswerClientInterface::answer() takes a new optional $conversationId and passes it to AI Answers' AnswerService. AnswerResult gains a turn property. In AiAnswersWorkflowRunner, WorkflowRunOptions::$continueRunId selects the conversation to continue. WorkflowRunOptions::$keepOpen is TRUE while a later question of the run follows this one, and it stops the runner deleting the conversation after the answer. A failed follow-up keeps the conversation id as its run id.

On a follow-up, the retrieve step is recorded as skipped ("follow-up: AI Answers does not search before the agent"), and the generate step is labeled Answer, turn N for turns after the first. The new WorkflowFollowUpInterface has one method, releaseRun(). The eval runner calls it after the last question of a chain, whether that question answered, failed or was skipped, so a conversation kept open for a follow-up that never ran is not left behind. It honors keep_conversation. Only runners that implement the interface receive follow-ups. The src/Service/EvalRunner.php changes that do the ordering and skip checks were not in the diff I could read, so the details of how the runner builds the judge transcript are not covered here.

The docs and tests describe these rules: a chain is linear, so two questions cannot follow the same question. The follow-up's input must be a string, not a message list. The question cannot follow itself. A run that is cancelled between two questions of a chain leaves the conversation stored until AI Answers' conversation_ttl expires it. The dataset schema adds metadata.follow_up_of as a non-empty string.

Upgrade

To ask a follow-up, name the earlier question in metadata.follow_up_of (from the docs):

questions:
  - id: q_entry
    input: "What are the entry requirements for the Marine Resource Management program?"
  - id: q_courses
    input: "Which courses does it include?"
    metadata:
      follow_up_of: q_entry

Custom workflow runners can implement Drupal\ai_eval\Workflow\WorkflowFollowUpInterface to receive follow-ups. Other runners skip them.

Summary

The ai_eval_flowdrop submodule previously told users the Drush command that makes a FlowDrop workflow synchronous would survive later saves in FlowDrop's editor. item.title: #3616124: Saving the anonymous user (uid 0) revokes access tokens for any consumer with an unset/anonymous default user
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 6.1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +661/−40 · php +661/−40
  • Diff: 721409f
  • Discussion: #3616124 · 9 contributors · 38 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 3 of 9 contributors

Summary

Saving the anonymous user (uid 0) no longer deletes OAuth tokens belonging to real users on consumers that have no default user. Saving a user who is a consumer's default user also no longer revokes other users' access tokens on that consumer. Tokens that actually authenticate as the saved user are still revoked, and refresh tokens are still kept. If you have custom code that relied on the old behavior of sweeping a default user's consumer tokens, use collectForClient() instead.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ExpiredCollector::collectForAccount() now returns only non-refresh tokens that authenticate as the account (explicit subject, or no/deleted subject on a Consumer defaulting to it) and returns [] for the anonymous account. TokenExpiryTriggerHandler::handleUserUpdate() ignores the anonymous account.

Technical details

simple_oauth_user_update() fires on every user save, including uid 0, and called ExpiredCollector::collectForAccount(). That method collected tokens by auth_user_id and then every token of any Consumer whose default user_id matched the account. The fix leaves the hook unchanged. TokenExpiryTriggerHandler::handleUserUpdate() now returns early for anonymous users, and collectForAccount() returns [] for them.

collectForAccount() now runs two queries. The first selects non-refresh tokens whose auth_user_id is the account. The second selects non-refresh tokens of Consumers defaulting to the account that have no existing user, using notExists('auth_user_id.entity.uid'). That covers tokens with no subject or a deleted subject, which fall back to the Consumer's default user. Tokens whose explicit subject is another existing user are skipped. The QueryException case when loading consumers by user_id now falls back to the first query's results only.

The collector queries in collect(), collectForAccount() and collectForClient() now use accessCheck(FALSE), since they are internal and not run on behalf of a user. The issue notes this means cron deletes expired tokens owned by any account. A reviewer found no query access handler on oauth2_token, so this was not filtering anything before. The anonymous skip lives in the default handler, which is a replaceable service from #2946882; a custom handler must add its own check. Refresh tokens are not revoked on user or consumer saves, consistent with #3436728, which rejects refresh grants for unpublished consumers.

Upgrade

If custom code called ExpiredCollector::collectForAccount() expecting every access token of a Consumer whose default user is the account, call collectForClient() for those consumers instead:

$tokens = $collector->collectForClient($consumer);

If you replaced the TokenExpiryTriggerHandlerInterface service, add your own $user->isAnonymous() check in handleUserUpdate().

  • Committed: November 6, 2026 (2 months later)

item.title: #3586785: HostnameFilter HTML-encodes & and > in Markdown output
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +437/−16 · php +412/−16 · md +25
  • Diff: 85d52a8
  • Discussion: #3586785 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

The AI module's hostname filter no longer turns & into & and > into > in text that has no HTML. Chat answers written in Markdown (quote blocks, code spans, tables) now come through unchanged. Plain-text mode no longer breaks Markdown links. A disallowed link is reduced to its text, and an allowed link keeps its closing parenthesis. Text that really does contain HTML tags is still filtered as before. An opt-in Markdown mode is available for consumers that render Markdown and want HTML examples inside code spans and blocks preserved.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New markdownMode property on HostnameFilterDto and new HostnameFilter::setMarkdownMode() method; snapshotSettings()/restoreSettings() now include markdownMode.

Technical details

The encoding came from HostnameFilter::filterText() always round-tripping text through the HTML5 parser, which encodes text nodes. After the Markdown link pass, it now returns early when the new containsHtmlMarkup() check finds no HTML. That check looks for < followed by a letter, /, ! or ?. It also treats invalid UTF-8 as HTML, because the HTML parser drops invalid bytes before tokenizing and so could hide a tag with an invalid byte after the < from the check. By default any <tag counts as markup, including inside backticks or indented code, since an HTML consumer would still act on it.

When markdownMode is TRUE, containsHtmlMarkup() parses the text with a League CommonMark parser, without rendering it. It reports HTML only if it finds an HtmlBlock, an HtmlInline, or a Text node containing a tag-like sequence. Autolinks, reference destinations and code therefore skip the HTML round trip. Plain-text mode takes precedence over Markdown mode. Mixed Markdown and HTML can still be HTML-encoded.

In plain-text mode, filterMarkdownLinks() now runs before the bare-URL pass, with $allow_rewrite = FALSE so a disallowed link is always reduced to its text and never rewritten. It also takes $preserve_mailto = TRUE, which keeps mailto: links, autolinks and reference definitions as plain-text mode already did for bare URLs. The bare-URL replacement now keeps trailing punctuation when it removes a URL. markdownMode is also handled by applySettings(), snapshotSettings() and restoreSettings(). The README gains a "Markdown consumers" section.

Upgrade

Only enable this if your consumer renders the output as Markdown:

use Drupal\ai\Dto\HostnameFilterDto;

$chatInput->setHostnameFilter(new HostnameFilterDto(markdownMode: TRUE));

For direct service calls, use $hostnameFilter->setMarkdownMode(TRUE). The service is shared, so restore the previous settings afterwards with snapshotSettings() and restoreSettings().

The target form now lists the workflows an engine can't run, with a reason. For FlowDrop the reason includes the Drush command that sets a synchronous orchestrator. The FlowDrop engine now has a proper label and checks the question port, fixed inputs, output path and an ignored provider or model when you save a target. Question port choices read "Title (name)", and a single allowed port is preselected. Steps on the results page show the canvas title with the node id. The README, the ai-eval skill and a new ai-eval-flowdrop skill document the extra FlowDrop modules a workflow needs and how to set the orchestrator.

It returns [id => ['label' => ..., 'reason' => ...]] and must never include anything listWorkflows() returns. EvalTargetForm calls it when the runner implements the interface. Summary

Workflow targets can now be created and edited in the AI Eval target form instead of only through YAML import. When at least one workflow runner is installed, the add form offers a Workflow mode. You pick the engine, then the workflow, then the input that receives the question. The lists refresh in place as you change the engine or workflow. You can also enter fixed inputs as YAML and set an output path. Chat provider and model settings now apply in workflow mode too, which AI Prompt needs. The form checks the engine, workflow, question port and fixed inputs on save, and shows a message if a runner fails to list its workflows or ports. Existing agent and chat targets cannot be switched to Workflow. Config YAML is still the export and import format.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New optional Drupal\ai_eval\Workflow\WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface (label(), questionPorts(), validateTarget()) and WorkflowRunnerCollector::label(). WorkflowRunnerInterface is unchanged.

Technical details

EvalTargetForm gains engine, workflow and question port selects with htmx redraws. A workflow with no declared ports gets a text field for the port. Per the shipped docs, the redraws go through the form's own route and permission, so no separate fragment routes were added. On save the form writes the workflow keys, keeps the stored workflow_snapshot (the form has no field for it), and returns form errors before the entity throws. Those errors cover an uninstalled engine, an unlisted workflow (a new check), an undeclared or disallowed question port, fixed inputs that name an undeclared port, and fixed inputs that name the question port.

The new optional WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface sits next to WorkflowRunnerInterface. label() gives the engine name. questionPorts($workflowId) returns the ports that can take the question, NULL for any declared port, or an empty list for none. validateTarget() takes the workflow id, question port, fixed inputs, output path, provider id and model id. It returns errors keyed by workflow_input_port, workflow_inputs, workflow_output_path or provider_model. A runner that implements only WorkflowRunnerInterface still works: WorkflowRunnerCollector::label() falls back to the engine id, and every declared port is allowed.

All four shipped runners implement the interface. AI Answers allows only question. Search API allows only keys. AI Automators allows every declared port except text_format. AI Prompt allows only declared variables that have a single-brace placeholder in the prompt. To keep save-time and run-time checks the same, each runner's run() checks were moved into shared private helpers (for example validateInputs() and validateModel()). PromptRenderer::validateValues() and UnsavedEntityBuilder::validateTextFormat() were extracted for the same reason. AI Automators now rejects a non-empty output path at save time. AI Prompt requires both a provider and a model. The docs in docs/user/usage/targets.md and docs/user/developers/index.md were updated.

Upgrade

final class MyRunner implements WorkflowRunnerInterface, WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface {
  public function label(): \Stringable {
    return new TranslatableMarkup('My engine');

  public function questionPorts(string $workflowId): ?array {

Runners that do not implement it keep working: the form shows the engine id and allows any declared port.
